record.original_question: In \mathbb{R}^3, consider a regular n-gon lying in the plane x = 1 and centered at (1, 0, 0). Let Q be the set of its vertices. Let f be a homothety with center at the origin and scale factor \lambda, where \lambda is small enough, and consider the terminal set \bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} f^k(Q). What is the structure of the Steiner tree connecting this terminal set?

evidence.quote:
Question 2.13. For a regular 3-dimensional n-gon in the plane x = 1 centered at (1, 0, 0); let Q be the set of its vertices
and consider the union of all f k (Q), k ∈ N, where f is a homothety with the center in the origin and a small enough scale
factor λ. What is the structure of the corresponding Steiner tree?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$. Fix an integer $n \geq 3$ and consider the regular $n$-gon that lies in the plane $\{x = 1\}$, is centered at the point $(1,0,0)$, and has a fixed circumradius (say $1$). Let $Q \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ denote the set of its $n$ vertices. For a real parameter $\lambda \in (0,1)$, let $f \colon \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be the homothety with center at the origin and ratio $\lambda$, i.e. $f(x) = \lambda x$. Define the terminal set
$$T_\lambda \;=\; \bigcup_{k \in \mathbb{N}} f^k(Q) \;\subset\; \mathbb{R}^3,$$
which is a countable set of points accumulating at the origin. A Steiner tree for $T_\lambda$ is a connected set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure containing $\overline{T_\lambda}$ (with the convention that, when no minimum exists, one considers infimizing sequences and their limits).

Problem: For all sufficiently small $\lambda > 0$, describe the structure of the Steiner tree connecting the terminal set $T_\lambda$. In particular, determine its combinatorial topology (the arrangement of Steiner points and edges), whether it is planar or genuinely three-dimensional, and whether it inherits a self-similar structure from the homothety $f$.
artifact.category_tag: Steiner trees on self-similar terminal sets
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a November 2025 collection of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers. Related results exist for Steiner trees on fractal/self-similar sets in the plane (e.g. self-similar binary trees, terminals on the sides of an angle), but no resolution of this specific 3D nonplanar case appears in the literature.

status_evidence.snippet: A collection of open questions on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers (November 2025).
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open questions in a recent compilation.

status_evidence.title: A Self-Similar Infinite Binary Tree Is a Solution to the Steiner Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Self-similar infinite binary tree shown to be a Steiner solution.
status_evidence.claim: Related self-similar Steiner results exist but in different (planar) settings.

status_evidence.title: On the Steiner tree connecting a fractal set
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Steiner trees connecting fractal point sets.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent work on Steiner trees for fractal terminals does not address the 3D regular n-gon homothety case.
